rationale: The mixed-timer receipt decided the point the source revision had left open, and it decided it positively: with a leader whose lease is 50ms and voters whose election timeout is 20ms, a competing leader appeared 21ms after the partition and the cut-off leader went on obtaining confirmations - ten of them - while that leader existed, with the two terms one apart. The uniform control in the same run produced no competing leader during the confirmation window at all. That restores the consequence half of the VerifyLeader finding for configurations whose nodes do not share timers, while leaving it bounded for uniform ones, and it means the account I recorded a few turns ago has to be corrected rather than merely extended. This update appends the child question's interpretation on its own receipt, revises the parent question's account with that receipt joined to its own, and closes the pause it was holding.

investigations.question: Across phases, how often does the cut-off leader's confirmation outlive the election of a competing leader when the cluster's nodes do not share timer settings, in contrast to the uniform case where the separation held in every trial?
investigations.hypothesis: Because the ordering between the confirmation window and a competing election follows from the per-node relation between the leader's lease and the voters' election timeout, the mixed configuration should show the overlap in essentially every trial while the uniform one should show none, provided each trial starts from a stable cluster whose timers are reset by the same leader.
investigations.discriminator: Repeat the mixed-timer trial twenty times and the uniform control twice, each on a fresh cluster, and compare the per-trial boolean that records whether any confirmation followed the appearance of a competing leader. The mixed case is expected to overlap throughout; the controls are expected to show no competing leader during the window.

interpretations.rationale: Retained execution (check dde7c68624b442d28c8d91b387f5e7bb, exit 0, tests_passed, 4 parsed events, 0 parse errors; two hand-built four-node clusters because the cluster helper cannot give nodes different settings). Comparison 0 holds and is complete on result index 1, admitted by the baseline at index 0: in the mixed-timer trial the leader carried a 50ms lease while the other voters carried a 20ms election timeout (both reported as operands in the same events), a competing leader appeared 21ms after the partition, and the cut-off leader still obtained 17 confirmations in total of which ten followed the appearance of that leader, with the leader at term 3 and the isolated node at term 4. Comparison 1 holds and is complete on result index 3, admitted by the baseline at index 2: with every node on the leader's settings no competing leader was observed during the confirmation window and no confirmation followed one. Read with the earlier twelve-trial receipt, which measured the same separation under uniform settings, the answer to the question is now split by configuration rather than open: under uniform settings the confirmation window closes before a competing leader can exist, and it closes for the reason the source revision gave (the lease check is the earliest event in the sequence because a peer cannot campaign until its own heartbeat timer expires); under settings that differ per node the ordering inverts and the confirmation outlives the election. The defect claim is asserted for the latter case: a caller that follows the documented pattern of consulting VerifyLeader before serving a read could be holding a confirmation obtained while a different leader had already been elected, which is exactly the condition the call exists to rule out. The mixed configuration is legal - ValidateConfig is applied per node - so the reachability question is whether operators end up with such a cluster, which is environmental rather than a library restriction; configuration drift or a partial rollout produces it.

knowledge.assertion: The cut-off leader kept confirming after a competing leader existed once a voter's election timeout was shorter than the leader's lease.

counterevidence: The overlap needs nodes with different settings; a cluster whose members share timers keeps the separation measured twelve times earlier, so the consequence is scoped to the mixed case rather than to VerifyLeader in general.
No application read is served in either run, so the overlap establishes that the confirmation coexisted with a competing leader, not that any particular stale value reached a client.
The competing leader's existence is read from the two isolated nodes' states, and its appearance time is bounded by the 2ms poll interval rather than observed exactly.
One mixed trial is the witness; the twelve-trial repetition measured the uniform case, not the mixed one, so the frequency of the overlap across phases is not established.
limitations: The mixed configuration uses one particular pair of timer sets (50ms lease against 20ms election), which brackets a range rather than enumerating it; the condition is an inequality between per-node values, which the run reports as an operand.
The clusters are single-process with in-memory transports, so partition timing is exact and no real network behaviour is involved.
The earlier uniform measurement stands unchanged and is what keeps this from being a general claim about VerifyLeader.
The witness is one trial; a frequency claim would need repetition of the mixed case, which this run did not do.

interpretations.rationale: Corrected account. The mechanism is unchanged and still rests on the parent's own receipt (check 89c0064015c643bdad64e7d81b492da5): the leader's tally is seeded with its own vote and incremented for every registered followerReplication, nonvoters included, while the quorum it is compared against counts only voters, so with three voters and one nonvoter the reachable nonvoter's acknowledgement completes the quorum of two. What changes with the mixed-timer receipt is the consequence, and it changes back in the direction the first revision of this account had claimed and the uniform measurement then bounded: with per-node timers a competing leader can be elected before the cut-off leader's confirmations stop, and in that run ten confirmations followed the appearance of a leader one term ahead. That is the stale-read basis the documented read pattern needs, and it is now witnessed rather than argued; the uniform case keeps the separation, so the accurate statement is that this defect's practical exposure depends on whether the cluster's nodes share their timer settings, which is an environmental condition the library permits rather than one it enforces. The three declared comparisons of the parent's own experiment, including the peerside observation that a detached majority committed an index the confirmed leader never applied, remain as recorded.

knowledge.assertion: The tally counts acknowledgements from every registered replication peer while the compared quorum counts voters only.
A leader whose only reachable peer is a nonvoter is confirmed against the voter quorum, and under per-node timers that confirmation can outlive a competing leader's election.

counterevidence: Uniform configurations bound the consequence: twelve trials measured the confirmation window closing before any competing leader, and the source path explains why, so the defect's practical exposure is not uniform across installations.
The defect is still scoped to clusters that contain a nonvoter, since the extra acknowledgement must come from a server whose suffrage is not Voter.
No application read is served in any of these runs; the claim is about the basis a read would rest on, not about an observed wrong value.
The mixed-timer witness is a single trial, so the frequency of the overlap is unknown.
limitations: One configuration per case (three voters plus one nonvoter, quorum two) with in-memory transports; the arithmetic generalizes over nonvoter presence, but only these cases were observed.
The mixed-timing case is legal but unusual, and the account does not estimate how often real clusters end up with such timers.

Whether the acknowledgement population should be voters only remains a design question for the target; this account states what the code does and what a caller relying on the documented read pattern gets.
The consequence evidence is one retained mixed trial joined to the parent's mechanism receipt; nothing here bounds the overlap's duration beyond the leader's lease.
interpretations.joint_history: The second receipt belongs to the child question's experiment rather than to this one, and it is compatible with this account because it observes the same object under the same construction: a leader cut off from every other voter but still able to reach a nonvoter, verified through the same channel the exported API uses, with the added variable of per-node timer settings. Its baseline events establish the same prerequisite (a healthy leader that verifies before the partition) and its exposure events carry the tally and quorum operands plus the timing values that classify the trial. The parent's own receipt remains the mechanism evidence - the tally reaching the voter quorum with the nonvoter as the only reachable peer - and the child receipt supplies the consequence that the parent's earlier revision had to bound.

scope.description: Twenty-two trials on hand-built four-node clusters, one fresh cluster per trial: twenty with per-node timers (the leader carrying a 50ms heartbeat, election and lease, the other nodes a 10ms heartbeat, 20ms election and 5ms lease) and two with every node on the leader's settings. Each trial forces leadership onto the slow node with a normal transfer, demotes one node to nonvoter, isolates the leader and that nonvoter from the two remaining voters in both directions, then verifies the leader repeatedly while reading whether either isolated node reports Leader.
assumptions: Per-node configurations are accepted by ValidateConfig, which is applied per node, so the mixed case is a legal cluster whose members drifted apart rather than a rejected one.
Each node is bootstrapped with the same configuration, as the target's own multi-node tests do.
The leader is forced onto the slow node by a normal LeadershipTransferToServer so the lease under test belongs to the leader.
Verification is driven through the same channel the exported API uses; a competing leader is detected by reading the two isolated nodes' states.
Trials start from a stable cluster whose follower timers were just reset by the leader's heartbeats; a partition landing during an already-running election is not part of this basis.
The dry run is native feedback only; the retained execution is what will be interpreted.
excluded: No application read is served; the measured quantity is whether a confirmation coexists with a competing leader, not what a client would receive.
No on-disk store, no network transport, no multi-process execution.
Only two timer sets are contrasted; the probe does not sweep configurations.

parameters.recorded_operands: leader_lease_ms, voter_election_ms, voter_election_shorter_than_lease, polls, confirmations, last_confirmation_ms, first_peer_leader_ms, confirmations_after_peer_leader, confirmation_after_peer_leader, leader_stepped_down, leader_term, peer_term, leader_applied_index

experiment.prefix: Unchanged from the single-witness harness apart from repetition: each trial builds four nodes by hand (an in-memory transport each, all pairs connected, one in-memory store serving as both log and stable store, an in-memory snapshot store and a MockFSM), bootstraps each node with the same configuration, starts each with its own Config, waits for any leader, transfers leadership to the slow node and waits until it reports Leader, demotes the fourth node with DemoteVoter, records a healthy baseline verification, applies one command, disconnects the leader and the nonvoter from the two remaining voters in both directions, then polls the verification path every 2ms while the leader still reports Leader and watches the two isolated nodes for a leader, emitting one summary event per trial with the counts, the last confirmation's elapsed time, the first competing leader's elapsed time, how many confirmations followed one, the terms and the configured timer values.

comparisons.description: Every mixed-timer trial shows at least one confirmation after a competing leader exists; any trial without one is reported as a witness, which is what makes the observed rate readable from the outcome.
Control: with every node on the leader's settings no confirmation follows a competing leader.
